1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 Sh. Jai Singh vs Union Of India on 12 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26228210/
1 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed LAC no. 234 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Singh v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 14 in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

sentences.text: The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar in possession of share in the land bearing Khasra no. 35/20 min (101), 42/23 min (112) total land admeasuring 2 Bigha 13 biswas having 1/2nd share and land comprised in khasra no. 35/12 min (04) having 1/6th share situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

It is stated that the petitioner was the absolute owner as well as in cultivatory possession of the said land and till the date of taking over the possession of the said land, the petitioner was having every right, title and interest in respect of the said land.
The said land is levelled and was having most productivity and fertility power and is fit for growing three crops in a year.
The said land is also free from any kind of pit and depression and was fit for using as residential site, industrial site and it hardly needs any LAC no. 234 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Jai Singh v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 14 development to be made upon it.

sentences.text: The petitioner was neither served with a notice prior to the announcement of the award as required under the law, nor the petitioner was supplied copy of the award despite request being made to this effect, therefore, the petitioner reserves its right to add, alter or delete the reference petition in respect of the said land.

6. It is stated that the compensation awarded by the learned LAC is inadequate and the ld. LAC has not taken into account the prevailing market rates as on the date of the notification passed under Section 4 of the Act, and the present petition has been filed on the following grounds.:
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method of valuation in determining the value of the said land and is totally based on the notification issued by the Government and thereby fixing the indicative price of the land for the purpose of acquisition of land in entire Delhi.

The price of the said land is always subject to change depending upon it situation and, therefore, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has quashed the earlier notification issued on 03.05.1994 for the purpose of stamping at Rs.
4,65,000 per acre.
(ii) The learned LAC, while assessing the market value of the said land has completely ignored the potential value of the said land.

All the civic facilities like the roads, electricity, hospital, telephones,
transport are situated in and around the said land and the said land is fit for residential, commercial and industrial purposes as on the passing of the notification under Section 4 of the act.

The best manner for determining the appropriate market value of the said land would be to get fixed by the Union of India vide various notifications.

and if, possible the deprived person should be given opportunity of being heard in deciding the price of the land.

State is a body of the representative for the welfare of the people and while doing so, the state or its organ is not supposed to gain anything in the name of compulsory acquisition, therefore,
the present reference petition has been filed in order to get the higher rate as awarded by the learned LAC.

(vi) The petitioner is also entitled for the market value which is assessed by the MCD for house tax and the surrounding area or at the rate on which the DDA is auctioning residential/commercial plots in the area or schedule of market rate of land in Delhi fixed by Union of India.

The policy decisions of NCT of Delhi fixing the market value of the land is only for agricultural land and thus fixing of market value is minimum indicative price and the land acquisition collector is free to reach at any higher market value

in order to determine the exact and correct compensation for the acquired land considering any other factor and circumstances which may fetch higher value or the above rates which has just been fixed by the learned LAC, however, the learned LAC has just followed the notification LAC no. 234 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Singh v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 14 of the government which shows minimum indicative price and in this way,
the learned LAC has not followed its mandatory duties.

The said land is surrounded by the posh colonies of DDA, therefore, the rates applicable on the non agricultural land will be applicable for determination of the market value of the said land.

The Union of India, GNCT of Delhi, MCD and DDA have acknowledged the effect of rise in the price of the said land, however, the NCT of Delhi by its various notifications,
administrative orders and policies.

Rise in prices of the land have also been acknowledged by the LAC time and again by way of making successive awards and through numerous judicial pronouncements and the Union of India by fixing schedule of market rates of the land in different areas of Delhi.

The learned LAC has assessed the market value of the said land by thumb rate method by simply adopting the rate of Government of NCT of Delhi and did not exercise to ascertain the real market value of the said land which is prevailing in the vicinity and essential for assessing the market value of the said land in the matter of compulsory acquisition of the land, even as per the rate fixed by the DDA for this land and nearby area, the rate of land are not less than Rs. 10,000 per square yards, however, the learned LAC has ignored the future prospects and possibilities of fetching much higher price for this land being its proximity with the welldeveloped the posh Colony, Rohini where the price of the land are not less than Rs. 20,000 per square yards.

The policy announcement which has been taken into consideration is dated 09.08.2001 and was made effective from 01.04.2001.

The notification under Section 4 of the Act was issued on 21.03.2003 i.e. almost two years later to the date of announcement of the policy, therefore, without prejudice to the other grounds, the learned LAC has not provided progressive increase of two years over and above Rs. 15,70,000.

(x) It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming compensation to the tune of Rs. 10,000/ per square yards and Rs. 1,00,000/ per acre may be given as severing charges.
Beside that Rs. 20.000/ may be given as damages and solatium @ 30% and further claim interest @ 9% and 15% as per the provisions of the Act.

submitted that the learned LAC has assessed the LAC no. 234 / 2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Jai Singh v. Union of India Page no. 8 of 14 value of the said land in respect of the true market value prevailing at the time of the notification.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is level to be dismissed with cost.

sentences.text: 13. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.
My issue wise findings and determination are as under :  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED TO ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF SO, TO WHAT AMOUNT ? OPP 14.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
LAC no. 234 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Singh v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 14 15.

Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
16. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

17. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

18. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.

There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the LAC no. 234 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Singh v. Union of India Page no. 12 of 14 land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).

19.
The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.

Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the Sh. Jai Singh vs Union Of India on 12 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26228210/

RELIEF 20.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioner is granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.
(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).

(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
